observation.visible_scene: Overhead close-up of a small open fire on dark, charred ground. A flattened cardboard box sits center-left, heavily engulfed in bright orange-yellow flames. Several crumpled white tissue/paper sheets lie around and on the box; some edges are already browned and burning. A small pink/magenta burned scrap with a tiny flame sits at the top center, and a vertical trail of white ash marks the soil to its right. The right half of the frame is rough blackened earth with scattered pale ash patches.
visible_changes: Flames continuously flicker, deform, and change height over the burning box and tissues throughout the whole excerpt (combustion already ongoing at the first frame).
The pre-existing white tissues on the left and bottom-left gradually brown, curl, and lose their white area as they burn.
Around the middle of the clip (frames ~26-32) a hand enters from the bottom-left holding a fresh, mostly-white folded paper sheet and lays it onto the burning box.
The newly placed sheet then begins to ignite: its edges darken and flames climb over it in the final frames (~33-41).
The pink/magenta scrap and the ash trail on the right remain essentially in place, with only their small flame flickering.

The framing drifts slightly so the burning box shifts a little toward the left edge and more charred ground appears on the right, indicating minor camera movement rather than the box itself translating.
outside_clip_unknowns: What or who started the fire and what the materials originally were.
The full extent of the scene beyond the close-up crop.
Whether the hand adds more paper after the last frame or how completely the added sheet burns.
uncertain_details: Exact material identities (tissue vs. paper vs. packaging) cannot be confirmed.
The direction and cause of the slight framing shift (camera pan/handheld drift) is uncertain from background cues alone.
Whether the small flame on the pink scrap is independent or spreading toward the main fire is not determinable.
